title: Enforcing post-mission disposal rules
bottleneck: The FCC now requires US satellites to deorbit within 5 years — tighter than the old 25-year interagency guideline — and ESA adopted similar rules, but enforcement is weak: no orbital police, penalties untested, and many operators face no consequences for non-compliance. The 25-year rule was based on 1990s models now judged insufficient, yet even stricter rules cover only new launches, doing nothing about the legacy population already in orbit.
why_it_blocks: Mitigation only works if everyone complies; a rule without enforcement is a suggestion, and the debris growth rate will not bend until compliance is near-universal and verified.
current_state: The FCC's 5-year rule (2022) applies to new US licenses; ESA's zero-debris charter pushes industry. Compliance tracking and penalties remain largely untested.
